rec.title: AWS Infrastructure Guide
rec.body:
This page documents how Harmony Games runs its backend on AWS. It complements the Architecture Overview (the big picture) and the Nakama Server Setup & Operations runbook (the game-server specifics). If you are new to the infra, read the Architecture Overview first, then come back here for the AWS-level detail.

We are a ten-person studio at this revision - seven paid staff plus three unpaid founders - down from a 2024 peak of 19 after the October 2025 reduction - so the guiding principle is managed over self-hosted. Almost everything below is a managed AWS service so we don't run a platform team. We bootstrapped the first two years largely on AWS Activate credits before we were paying list price.

Account & region layout

Accounts are split under Control Tower by title and by environment, and inconsistently: Domino Delights has separate dev and prod accounts, Zombie Match 3D uses one account for both (separated only by region), and the analytics pipeline has its own account shared by QA and prod. Region assignment is per component rather than one primary: the Zombie Match 3D backend is us-west-2 in prod and us-east-2 in dev, the Domino Delights backend is us-east-2 in prod, and the analytics pipeline runs in us-east-2. us-east-2 is a live environment, not a DR footprint. Everything sits inside a multi-AZ VPC (three availability zones), with public subnets for the load balancer and private subnets for compute and data.

Services in use

LayerAWS serviceWhat it does for us
ComputeECS FargateRuns the containerized Phoenix API and the Nakama game server. No EC2 hosts to patch.
DatabaseAurora PostgreSQLPrimary transactional store for player state, economy and live-ops config. Aurora Serverless v2, single writer, no read replicas. Non-standard port 5433.
IngressApplication Load BalancerEach stack has its own public ALB on its own hostname - Phoenix, Nakama and the Domino Delights Node service are not behind a shared load balancer.
CertificatesACMTLS certs for each title's own game domain, auto-renewed and attached to each ALB. harmonygames.co is the marketing site only.
Event lakeS3Raw client and server events land here as the analytics data lake.
Streaming / ETLKinesis + GlueKinesis ingests the event firehose; Glue jobs transform and partition it in S3, where a Glue crawler catalogues the processed prefix so Athena can query it in place. The reporting layer itself is BigQuery + Metabase; the Snowflake replica is a separate hand-refreshed copy (see the analytics integration page).
ObservabilityCloudWatch + X-RayContainer logs, alarms and dashboards (CloudWatch) plus X-Ray traces on the identity-component Lambdas, the quests Lambdas, the analytics-pipeline Lambdas and the Domino Delights Node service (X-Ray daemon sidecar). The Elixir/Phoenix backend and Nakama are not traced.

Analytics pipeline

The event path is worth calling out because it spans two regions. Clients and the game server emit events; those are written into Kinesis streams, dropped to S3 in raw form, and then Glue crawls and ETLs them into the curated tables our warehouse reads. This is the AWS half of the flow; the warehouse side lives on the analytics team's docs.

  • us-west-2 - game backend and Aurora. (Analytics ingestion is NOT here: the analytics CDK stack is single-region us-east-2 for both QA and prod.)
  • us-east-2 - Glue jobs, curated S3, cross-region backup copies.

Deploys

Service images are built locally by cdk deploy and pushed to ECR from a developer machine, then rolled out to the relevant Fargate service with a rolling update behind the ALB health checks. CI runs lint and tests only - it does not deploy any service. The one CI-driven deploy in the org is the marketing site's S3 sync (website/.github/workflows/s3-deploy*.yml). There is no manual SSH step - a failed health check rolls the task back automatically.

Cost note (estimates only). These are rough monthly figures pulled from Cost Explorer for planning; treat them as directional, not billing-accurate.

  • Fargate (Phoenix + Nakama): ~$650/mo
  • Aurora Serverless v2 (single writer): ~$420/mo
  • S3 + Kinesis + Glue (analytics): ~$300/mo
  • ALB + data transfer + CloudWatch/X-Ray: ~$180/mo

The single biggest lever is right-sizing Fargate task memory - check the CloudWatch utilization dashboard before bumping a task definition.

Ownership

Infra was owned by Douglas (Engineering, departed Oct 2025); with the team wound down, changes now go through the remaining executive owner. If you need a new IAM role, a subnet change, or a new Glue job, open an ENG ticket and tag it infra - do not click around in the console for anything that touches production networking.

Service inventory

There is no single production account and no single primary region: every CDK stack takes account and region from CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT / CDK_DEFAULT_REGION at deploy time, and the npm deploy scripts set them per title and per environment (see the account & region layout above). Compute is containerised on ECS Fargate; state is Aurora PostgreSQL; the analytics path is Kinesis → Glue → S3.

ServiceAWS primitiveNotes
Game APIECS FargateElixir/Phoenix; autoscaled on CPU utilization (target 80%, 3-10 tasks) behind an ALB
Social / accountsECS Fargate (Nakama)client API 7350 / HTTP admin 7351 behind an HTTPS ALB; 7349 is exposed in local dev only
Primary datastoreAurora PostgreSQLAurora Serverless v2, single writer, no read replicas; automated snapshots
Event streamKinesis Data StreamsClient telemetry ingestion; feeds Glue
ETLAWS GlueBatches Kinesis records to partitioned Parquet in S3
LakeS3Partitioned by event date; the BI warehouse loads from here

Scaling & limits

Fargate services scale horizontally; Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity units with load; there is no reader endpoint. Concurrency was never instrumented: the ~1K figure in the Google Drive sheet “Domino Delights _ Beta Launch Readiness_” (tab Beta Checklist, row 26) was a peak-CCU launch target, not a measurement, and it is CCU rather than DAU. Peak measured DAU was ~1,240 (Domino Delights, late June 2025). Cost, not capacity, has been the constraint.

Cost control: non-prod runs at reduced capacity rather than zero (a dev Fargate floor of 1-2 tasks and an Aurora Serverless v2 minimum of 0.5 ACU); the Kinesis stream is provisioned with a single shard. The AWS activation credits materially offset the first year of spend.

Deploy & rollback

Infrastructure is AWS CDK; application deploys are rolling on Fargate with health-check gating. Rollback is redeploy of the previous task-definition revision.

Disaster recovery

Aurora automated backups + manual pre-release snapshots; S3 is versioned and the lake is reproducible from Kinesis replay within the retention window. RPO is the snapshot cadence; RTO is dominated by Aurora restore time.

FailureMitigationRecovery
Writer AZ lossAurora Serverless v2, single writer - no standby instanceAWS restarts the writer in a healthy AZ from the shared cluster volume; expect minutes of downtime, not a sub-minute failover. (Domino Delights' Nakama RDS instance is separately multi-AZ and does fail over.)
Bad migrationPre-release snapshotRestore snapshot; replay Kinesis
Accidental S3 deleteBucket versioningRestore prior version

On-call

Alarms page the two-person rota via the on-call tool. The first responder triages; anything touching Aurora or a data migration escalates to Arthur Blake before any write action.
